title: Agent wait heuristics: replace sleep/poll loops with event-driven BRC message stream consumption
summary: Architecture analysis for Option C (full scope per HITL resolution). Revision 3 reconciles with the task_planner's already-CONFIRMED plan: the consensus_wrapper uses SSE (curl --no-buffer against the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED event emitted by orchestrator/sse.py), NOT a new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED; the agent preamble uses the canonical `egg-orch message wait-loop --for <TYPE>` idiom keyed off the existing MessageType.CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED. TD-8 (new MessageType) is DELETED — the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED at events.py:67 already handles the wrapper case without a new bus type. Tracks collapse to six: prompt audit + single-idiom docs, configurable --wait cap, typed blocking primitive + wait-loop, in-memory store blocking, HEARTBEAT + HealthMonitor + QUESTION removal, consensus_wrapper SSE rewrite, and WSGI worker-model deployment track.

reviewer_plan_revision_2_nacks.summary: TD-5/Track 6 (message wait for wrapper + new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED) conflict with the already-CONFIRMED plan's Phase 5 (SSE via curl --no-buffer on EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED). Plan's SSE design was the task_planner's response to RISK-6 (load-bearing for local dev without Redis) and RISK-7 (SIGTERM via socket close). Two different mechanisms cannot both ship.
reviewer_plan_revision_2_nacks.resolution: Adopted reviewer's recommended option (b): DEFER to the task_planner's already-CONFIRMED SSE design. (1) TD-5 rewritten to endorse SSE via curl --no-buffer against orchestrator/sse.py's EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED; (2) Track 6 rewritten to mirror plan Phase 5 (TASK-5-1 verbatim references); (3) TD-8 DELETED — the new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED is no longer needed because the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED at events.py:67 (SSE event-name) already fires on final consensus and curl --no-buffer honours SIGTERM cleanly; (4) Track 5 no longer adds a MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED — only HEARTBEAT (new) and QUESTION (removal); (5) TD-7's preamble example updated to match plan's TASK-6-1 idiom: `egg-orch message wait-loop --for CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED --for CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW --for OVERSEER_ALERT` (note: wait-loop is the convenience CLI added by plan TASK-2-4 that wraps message wait with exit-code handling). CONSENSUS_REACHED as a MessageType is noted as a deferred option for future agent consumers if they ever need type-filtered consensus detection outside the SSE channel — not in scope for this issue.

problem_statement.description: During pipeline issue-1762-membump (2026-04-22) multiple agents used sleep/poll anti-patterns that blackholed them for 5-10 minutes while actionable messages (NACKs, overseer nudges, peer proposals) sat unread in their inboxes. Root cause is a combination of (a) the BRC preamble's 'Keep polling' phrasing in pipelines.py:5959 and :6020 which nudges LLMs toward outer `for i in 1..N; do egg-orch message poll --wait 60; done` loops, (b) the 60-second hard cap on `--wait` in routes/messages.py:165 which forces *some* outer loop no matter what, (c) the absence of a typed 'wait for specific event' primitive so agents default to generic poll loops, (d) silent non-blocking fallback in the in-memory message store (routes/messages.py:181-184) that defeats `--wait > 0` in local/CI deploys, and (e) the absence of a heartbeat message type so overseer liveness inference relies on message timing rather than explicit state.
goals: Agents react to bus events in seconds, not minutes — bounded by reasoning latency, not sleep heuristics
BRC consensus turn-around is dominated by actual producer work, not agent-side wait loops
Overseer liveness inference reads explicit agent state (HEARTBEAT) rather than inferring from message timing
Local development and CI (in-memory store backend) exercise the same blocking semantics as production (Redis)
consensus_wrapper's own stay-alive loop is event-driven so it has the same cache-cost / latency profile as the agents it wraps
One canonical recommended idiom per wait scenario — no variance across agents
non_goals: Introduce a REQUEST/REPLY peer-addressed messaging subsystem to replace QUESTION (explicitly deferred per decision-5 HITL resolution)
Change SSE streaming or the /events endpoint shape
Refactor the BRC protocol state machine itself — only the wait primitives around it
Backward-incompatible changes to the message store schema or existing CLI flags
Add a new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED — the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED on SSE is sufficient for the wrapper case (per revision 3 reconciliation with plan Phase 5)

findings.title: 'Keep polling' preamble language causes LLM-driven outer loops
findings.description: The producer and reviewer lifecycle steps both end with 'STAY ALIVE: Keep polling egg-orch message poll --wait 30 until the orchestrator stops you.' This reads as a recurring action the agent must orchestrate. Combined with LLM training data rich in `for i in ...; do ...; done` and `while true; do ...; sleep N; done` idioms, it produces the exact anti-patterns observed in issue-1762-membump.
findings.remediation: Replace preamble with the canonical idiom per plan TASK-6-1: `egg-orch message wait-loop --for CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED --for CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW --for OVERSEER_ALERT` (single invocation). Add explicit Don'ts listing for-loop wrapping and `sleep N`. Covered in Track 1 = plan Phase 6.

findings.title: 60s hard cap on --wait forces outer loops even for correct agents
findings.description: routes/messages.py:165 caps `wait` at 60s via `min(max(int(...), 0), 60)`. Even an agent that correctly uses `--wait 60` without a loop still has its connection close every 60s.
findings.remediation: Make the cap configurable via `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` (default 60s). Track 2 = plan Phase 2 (TASK-2-3).

findings.title: No typed 'wait for specific event' primitive
findings.description: Agents currently have `egg-orch message poll --wait N` (generic bulk fetch) and nothing else. When an agent wants to wait for specific events it must wrap in a loop and manually filter.
findings.remediation: Introduce `egg-orch message wait --for TYPE [--from ROLE] [--timeout N]` (decision-2) plus the `wait-loop` convenience wrapper (plan TASK-2-4) that handles retries and exit codes. Covered in Track 3 = plan Phase 2 (TASK-2-1, TASK-2-2, TASK-2-4).

findings.title: In-memory store silently falls back to non-blocking — breaks local dev and CI
findings.description: routes/messages.py:181-184 catches TypeError when `wait` kwarg is rejected. Q2 HITL confirms local deploys run without Redis, so this is load-bearing for dev.
findings.remediation: Add a per-pipeline threading.Condition to InMemoryMessageStore (plan TASK-1-1). clear() must also notify_all. Track 4 = plan Phase 1.

findings.title: No HEARTBEAT message type — overseer infers liveness from message timing
findings.description: No structured state heartbeat. Overseer Tier 1 inferences conflate 'alive but correctly waiting' with 'stalled'. Additionally, HealthMonitor._on_message_sent at line 330-360 does NOT reset last_heartbeat — so HEARTBEAT adopters would still trip heartbeat_timeout at line 400-460.
findings.remediation: Add MessageType.HEARTBEAT with structured state field. Wire HealthMonitor._on_message_sent to reset last_heartbeat on HEARTBEAT (plan TASK-3-3). Hard rate limit at send_message. Track 5 = plan Phase 3.

findings.title: consensus_wrapper's own stay-alive loop mirrors the agent anti-pattern
findings.description: consensus_wrapper.py:322-351 runs a 30s-sleep shell while-loop (10 cycles × 30s = 300s).
findings.remediation: Per plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1, rewrite with `curl --no-buffer` against orchestrator/sse.py's existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED (SSE event-name 'consensus.reached'). No new MessageType needed — the SSE event-name already distinguishes final from pending. curl honours SIGTERM via socket close. Shell-sleep fallback when SSE endpoint is unreachable (preserves zero-Redis local-dev path). Track 6 = plan Phase 5.

findings.title: QUESTION message type has 11+ call sites across production, tests, and docs
findings.description: QUESTION is not merely a test-fixture type — 4 production sites (enum, BRC_HISTORY_TYPES, reviewer-preamble active advertisement, CLI), 6 test-file references, 1 docs reference. Reviewer preamble advertisement means removing the type without removing the preamble causes runtime errors.
findings.remediation: Track 5 (bundled with HEARTBEAT) = plan Phase 7, which stages removal in 4 commits in safe order: prompt edit first (so the preamble no longer advertises the removed type), then BRC_HISTORY_TYPES, then 5 test files, then enum removal.

findings.title: mission.md polling guidance is minimal and not surfaced in preamble
findings.description: sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md:152 says 'Use egg-orch message poll --wait 30 for long-polling (not sleep loops)' but does not explain WHY, does not name a single idiom, and does not prohibit for-loops.
findings.remediation: Create `docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md` per plan Phase 8 (TASK-8-1) with the single recommended idiom, explicit Don'ts, and a 'why' paragraph. Track 1 = plan Phases 6+8.

recommended_approach.name: Option C — Six architectural tracks aligned to task_planner's 9-phase plan
recommended_approach.alignment_note: This architecture analysis was revised to align with the task_planner's already-CONFIRMED plan (.egg-state/drafts/1897-plan.md, 9 phases). The tracks below map 1:N onto plan phases; the plan is the source of truth for implementation steps, acceptance criteria, and file-level tasks. Architect tracks exist only to document architectural rationale, risk mitigations, and HITL traceability.

tracks.name: Prompt audit + single-idiom docs
tracks.scope: Rewrite BRC preamble STAY ALIVE steps per plan TASK-6-1 with canonical idiom `egg-orch message wait-loop --for CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED --for CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW --for OVERSEER_ALERT`. Update mission.md per TASK-6-2. Write docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md per TASK-8-1.
depends_on: plan Phase 7 (QUESTION removal for reviewer preamble)
tracks.architectural_rationale: F1, F8. LLMs follow explicit imperative instructions better than 'keep polling' descriptive phrasing.

tracks.name: Configurable --wait cap
tracks.scope: Plan TASK-2-3. Replace literal 60 in routes/messages.py:165 with `int(os.environ.get('EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT', '60'))`. Startup warning when value > 90s (per plan, naming gateway Squid ConfigMap key).
tracks.architectural_rationale: F2, RISK-4. 60s cap forces outer loops; env-configurable with default preserves behavior.

tracks.name: Typed blocking primitive + wait-loop convenience CLI
tracks.scope: Plan TASK-2-1 (message wait HTTP route + Redis helper), TASK-2-2 (message wait CLI with --for/--from/--timeout and exit-code contract 0/1/2/3 per TD-10), TASK-2-4 (message wait-loop convenience wrapper that encapsulates the retry+exit-code handling so the prompt can ship a one-liner).

tracks.name: In-memory store true blocking
tracks.scope: Plan TASK-1-1 (per-pipeline threading.Condition in InMemoryMessageStore with notify_all in both add_message AND clear) + TASK-1-3 (remove silent non-blocking fallback at routes/messages.py:181-184). Blocking loop re-checks pipeline_id after wake.

tracks.name: HEARTBEAT type + HealthMonitor wiring + QUESTION removal
tracks.scope: Phase 3: add MessageType.HEARTBEAT + HEARTBEAT rate limit at send_message (hard 429, EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT default 20/min) + extend HealthMonitor._on_message_sent at health_monitor.py:330-360 to reset last_heartbeat on HEARTBEAT (plan TASK-3-3). Phase 7: remove QUESTION in 4 staged commits (prompt edit at pipelines.py:6062-6074 first, then BRC_HISTORY_TYPES at :4775, then 5 test files, then enum removal).
tracks.architectural_rationale: F5, F7, RISK-1, RISK-2, RISK-10. CONSENSUS_REACHED as a MessageType is NOT added this pipeline — the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED on SSE is sufficient for the wrapper case; agent-bus consumers can use the existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED type (wait-loop wakes on both flavours and status-check decides).

tracks.name: consensus_wrapper SSE rewrite
tracks.scope: Plan TASK-5-1. Rewrite consensus_wrapper.py:322-351 to event-block via `curl --no-buffer --silent $ORCH_URL/api/v1/pipelines/$PIPELINE_ID/events | while read line; do ... done` parsing SSE events for `event: consensus.reached` (EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED at events.py:67, emitted by orchestrator/sse.py). Compute timeout from existing MAX_READY_POLLS × EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_INTERVAL budget. Fall back to current shell sleep loop on SSE 5xx or connection refused (no-Redis local-dev path preserved per RISK-6). SIGTERM handler: `trap 'kill $CURL_PID 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM`. Preserve existing exit-code classification (134/136/137/139/255 → transient).
tracks.architectural_rationale: F6, RISK-6, RISK-7, RISK-11. SSE approach has three advantages over message wait: (1) wrapper is shell-native and curl --no-buffer is idiomatic shell; (2) event-name 'consensus.reached' already distinguishes final from pending without MessageType changes; (3) falls back gracefully to shell sleep loop when Redis/orchestrator unavailable (local-dev).

tracks.name: WSGI worker model + operator guide
tracks.scope: Plan Phase 4 (TASK-4-1, TASK-4-2, TASK-4-3). Switch Gunicorn to gevent workers, 2× cap timeout, dedicated /healthz probe off worker pool, egg_inflight_long_polls metric. Document EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT × worker-count coupling.
tracks.architectural_rationale: RISK-3. Must ship before Track 3/6 go live in production.

recommended_approach.rationale_for_order: Plan's phase numbering is the canonical merge order. Architect tracks defer to plan phases for sequencing.

Option B — blocking primitive + prompts + docs, defer heartbeats

alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Per Q4 HITL resolution (dedicated HEARTBEAT type).

Add a new MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED bus-side mirror of the SSE EventType
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Considered in revision 2 but superseded in revision 3 per reviewer_plan NACK: the task_planner's already-CONFIRMED Phase 5 uses SSE (curl --no-buffer on the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED) which does not require a new MessageType. Future agent-bus consumers can use the existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED MessageType (filtered via wait-loop) if they need type-filtered bus-side detection.

alternatives_considered.name: Wrapper uses egg-orch message wait CLI (MessageType-filtered) instead of SSE
alternatives_considered.rejected_reason: Considered in revision 2 but superseded in revision 3: (a) wrapper is shell script, curl --no-buffer is idiomatic; (b) SSE event-name already distinguishes final from pending (no MessageType schema change needed); (c) SSE fallback to shell sleep loop on Redis-down is simpler than Redis-required message wait. Plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1 is the chosen implementation.

technical_decisions.title: Server-side typed wait is a loop over XREAD BLOCK, not a new Redis structure
technical_decisions.rationale: XREAD BLOCK with Python-side type/role filtering already works.
technical_decisions.implications: get_messages(..., wait=N) returns all matching messages; the new wait_for_typed helper filters inside the server loop.

technical_decisions.title: In-memory blocking uses threading.Condition (per-pipeline), not threading.Event
technical_decisions.rationale: Multiple waiters; role/type filtering happens after wake. Condition + notify_all is canonical.
technical_decisions.implications: InMemoryMessageStore gains per-pipeline `_cond = threading.Condition(self._lock)`. add_message and clear both notify_all. Blocking loop re-checks pipeline_id after wake (RISK-5).

technical_decisions.title: HEARTBEAT state is emitted on transitions, not periodically — with HARD rate limit at send_message
technical_decisions.rationale: Periodic heartbeats recreate bus pollution. Transition-based emission bounds count by state-change events.
technical_decisions.implications: Agents emit on: start (WORKING), work done (PROPOSED/IDLE), waiting on peer (WAITING_ON_ROLE), consensus (CONFIRMED). Send_message returns 429 above EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT (default 20/min). HealthMonitor._on_message_sent resets last_heartbeat on HEARTBEAT (plan TASK-3-3) — REQUIRED consumer change.

technical_decisions.title: QUESTION removal is staged in 4 commits (not atomic) per plan Phase 7
technical_decisions.rationale: Plan's staged approach (prompt → BRC_HISTORY_TYPES → tests → enum) avoids runtime errors if any stage fails mid-commit.
technical_decisions.implications: 11 call sites touched across 4 commits. Reviewer-preamble edit lands FIRST so the preamble no longer advertises QUESTION before the type is removed. See F7 / RISK-1 / RISK-10.

technical_decisions.title: consensus_wrapper uses SSE (curl --no-buffer against EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED), NOT a new MessageType
technical_decisions.rationale: Revision 3 reconciliation with task_planner plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1. SSE approach has three advantages: (a) wrapper is shell-native, curl is idiomatic; (b) existing SSE event-name 'consensus.reached' at orchestrator/sse.py already distinguishes final from pending (no MessageType schema change); (c) graceful fallback to shell sleep loop on SSE 5xx or Redis-down (load-bearing for local dev per RISK-6).
technical_decisions.implications: consensus_wrapper.py:322-351 rewritten per plan TASK-5-1. curl --no-buffer; trap 'kill $CURL_PID 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM; fall back to shell sleep loop on connection failure. Exit-code classification unchanged. Budget computed from existing MAX_READY_POLLS × EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_INTERVAL.

technical_decisions.title: Env var naming — EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT, EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT
technical_decisions.implications: Defaults preserve behavior (60s cap, 20/min HB rate). Startup warn above 90s for cap.

technical_decisions.title: Preamble wording: canonical `wait-loop` idiom, not raw `message wait`
technical_decisions.rationale: Plan TASK-2-4 adds `egg-orch message wait-loop` convenience wrapper that encapsulates retry+exit-code handling. Single one-liner for the prompt; LLMs do not need to learn shell error handling.
technical_decisions.implications: Final preamble text per plan TASK-6-1: 'STAY ALIVE: Run `egg-orch message wait-loop --for CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED --for CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW --for OVERSEER_ALERT` once. The command blocks server-side until a matching message arrives or EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT elapses, retries transient errors with backoff, and exits cleanly when consensus is reached. Do NOT use for i in 1..N. Do NOT call sleep N. Do NOT issue redundant egg-orch consensus confirmed calls.'

technical_decisions.title: [DELETED] New MessageType.CONSENSUS_REACHED
technical_decisions.rationale: Revision 3: deleted per reviewer_plan NACK blocking-1-rev2. The existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED on SSE (events.py:67) is sufficient for the wrapper case per plan TASK-5-1. Adding a new MessageType was a revision-2 design that conflicted with the already-CONFIRMED plan. The wrapper uses SSE; agent-bus consumers use existing CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED (wait-loop wakes and the agent checks consensus status).

technical_decisions.title: message wait + --since for resumability (implementer discretion)
technical_decisions.rationale: Transport-error retry must not double-deliver. Plan TASK-2-4's wait-loop wrapper handles transport retry internally; the raw `message wait --for` may not need --since if wait-loop tracks since-IDs across retries.
technical_decisions.implications: Plan TASK-2-2 currently lists --for/--from/--timeout only. If the implementer finds a case where the raw wait is called by code outside wait-loop and needs resumability, --since can be added — otherwise defer.

technical_decisions.title: message wait exit codes (0/1/2/3)
technical_decisions.rationale: Wrapper (track-6 = plan Phase 5) and wait-loop (plan TASK-2-4) need deterministic exit-code contract.
technical_decisions.implications: 0 = match found; 1 = timeout with no match; 2 = transient connection failure (retry with backoff); 3 = permanent error (4xx, authz). Codified in plan TASK-2-2.

constraints: No backwards-incompatible bus schema change for in-flight pipelines — additions (HEARTBEAT) are safe; removal of QUESTION is staged in 4 commits starting with the prompt edit so agents never encounter a runtime error.
